classification.difficultyReason: Convert bearings on opposite sides of north to triangle angles before the two range calculations.

content.prompt:
A ship is located at $B$ and two radar stations 75 km apart are located at $A$ and $C$.
The bearing of the ship from one radar station is $038^\circ$ and from the other radar station it is $306^\circ$.
$C$ is due east of $A$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5, diagram below parts a and b
spec.description: Blue triangle ABC with horizontal AC, A left, C right and B above between them. Separate dark north arrows at A and C are labelled North. Small bearing arc at A reads 38 degrees. Clockwise reflex arc at C reads 306 degrees below the arc and ends with an arrow towards CB. No length is printed on AC.
spec.mathematics: Bearing AB=038 degrees; bearing CB=306 degrees; C due east of A. Source triangle strokes #014D85. Derived interior angles and distances must not appear.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How far is the ship from the radar station at $A$, to the nearest kilometre?

children.label: b
children.prompt: How far is the ship from the radar station at $C$, to the nearest kilometre?
